properties.query:
SigninLogs
| where ResultType != "0"
| where isnotempty(UserPrincipalName)
| summarize TargetedAccounts = dcount(UserPrincipalName), Accounts = make_set(UserPrincipalName, 25),
    Attempts = count(), StartTime = min(TimeGenerated), EndTime = max(TimeGenerated)
    by IPAddress, Location
| where TargetedAccounts >= 5
| extend TimeGenerated = EndTime, IP = IPAddress
properties.displayName: Identity - Password Spray from Single Source IP
properties.description:
DETECTS
A single source IP producing failed sign-ins against five or more distinct accounts within an hour.

WHY IT MATTERS
Password spraying inverts brute force: one or two common passwords tried against many accounts, staying under per-account lockout thresholds. Because no single account looks unusual, it is invisible to per-user detections and is the most common route into cloud tenants (MITRE T1110, Brute Force).

TRIAGE
1. Check whether ANY account from the same IP subsequently succeeded. That is the critical question.
2. Geolocate the IP and assess whether it is plausible for your user base.
3. Review the account list for a pattern, such as sequential or harvested-from-public naming.
4. If a success occurred, treat that account as compromised and pivot to its post-auth activity.
5. Block the IP at Conditional Access and confirm smart lockout is enabled.

FALSE POSITIVES
A shared corporate NAT gateway after a mass password expiry, or a misconfigured application retrying stored credentials for multiple users. Both show low IP diversity and a benign pattern on inspection.

SOURCE
SigninLogs
